resources.string: How an astrocyte supports a synapse
Normal support around one excitatory synapse. The paths are schematic and not to scale.
Glutamate carries the message from one neuron to the next. A nearby astrocyte has branches alongside the synapse and an endfoot resting against a capillary.
After the signal, a nearby astrocyte branch takes up some of the released glutamate, helping clear it from the space around the synapse.
Inside the astrocyte, some of the captured glutamate is converted to glutamine.
Glutamine passes back to the sending neuron, which can turn it into glutamate for future messages. This return is recycling, not a new signal.
The astrocyte also takes up some potassium from the space around active neurons, helping limit local changes in potassium levels.
